help:
Land use and land cover change modelling

Usage: terraflux [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  app          Open the application (with a model, if given)
  run          Run a model and write its outputs
  check        Check a model and its data without running it
  ops          List the operators (`--json`: their full signatures)
  new          Create a model from a classic land change model
  convert      Write a model in another format (by the extension: .toml or .json)
  mcp          A server of the Model Context Protocol on the standard input and output: an AI assistant (Claude, Gemini CLI, Codex...) builds, checks and runs models through it; the application, with the model open, shows its edits as they are made
  serve        Run a coordinator: workers ask it for tasks, clients submit batches to it
  worker       Run a headless worker: tasks from a coordinator, until stopped
  workers      The workers of a coordinator and what they do
  jobs         The jobs of a coordinator, done or not
  results      Follow a job of a coordinator to its end and write its files (those written already kept)
  submit       Run a batch of a model: replicates (one seed each) or scenarios, here or on a coordinator's workers
  calibrate    Calibrate settings of a model against an observed map, here or on a coordinator's workers
  sensitivity  A global sensitivity analysis of a model's output to its settings (Morris or Sobol, as SALib), here or on a coordinator's workers
  cluster      Clusters and servers reached by SSH: saved once, used by `submit --on`, `calibrate --on`, `results --on`
  cloud-init   The setup script (cloud-init user data) of a machine rented in the cloud: a server with Terraflux (then `terraflux cluster add`), or, with --worker, a machine working for a server's coordinator
  resample     Resample a raster to the grid of another (of the same coordinate reference system)
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --threads <THREADS>  Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version

run.help:
Run a model and write its outputs

Usage: terraflux run [OPTIONS] <MODEL>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  The model (.toml or .json)

Options:
  -o, --out <OUT>                  The folder of the outputs (default: `output` next to the model)
      --threads <THREADS>          Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --set <NAME=VALUE>           Replace an input (`name=path` for a file, `name=value` (JSON) for a value) or a node's setting (`node.setting=value`); e.g. `--set seed=7`, `--set patches.isometry=2`
  -q, --quiet                      Print only errors
      --tiled                      Run on tiles (maps larger than memory; Dinamica EGO's model): the same maps with any number of threads or machines (the tile size changes the patches a fit measures), statistically equivalent to the exact engine
      --tile <TILE>                The side of the tiles (cells) [default: 1024]
      --radius <RADIUS>            The largest distance of a patch's cell from its seed (cells) [default: 32]
      --disk <DISK>                Keep the steps' layers in this folder instead of memory
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  Run the tiles on a coordinator's workers (with --tiled and --disk): the maps and the layers' tiles go to them through the coordinator
      --code <CODE>                The coordinator's pairing code
      --shared-disk                The workers read the model's files and --disk on storage they share with this machine, at the same paths (only sums travel)
  -h, --help                       Print help

new.help:
Create a model from a classic land change model

Usage: terraflux new [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  dinamica  Dinamica EGO's classic model: Markov rates, weights of evidence, Expander and Patcher
  clue      CLUE-S (lulcc's CluesModel): logistic regressions, a linear demand, CLUE allocation
  ordered   The ordered allocation (lulcc's OrderedModel): logistic regressions, a linear demand
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --threads <THREADS>  Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
  -h, --help               Print help

subcommands.dinamica:
Dinamica EGO's classic model: Markov rates, weights of evidence, Expander and Patcher

Usage: terraflux new dinamica [OPTIONS] --t0 <T0> --t1 <T1> --drivers <DRIVERS> --steps <STEPS> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --t0 <T0>                      The map at the start of the calibration period: `file.tif` or `file.tif:band` (a name or a 0-based index)
      --threads <THREADS>            Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --t1 <T1>                      The map at its end
      --drivers <DRIVERS>            The drivers: a raster with one band per variable
      --steps <STEPS>                Time steps in the calibration period
      --simulate <SIMULATE>          Steps to simulate (default: `steps`)
      --start <START>                The map the simulation starts from (default: t0)
      --increment <INCREMENT>        The weights' buffer increment (default: a hundredth of each variable's range)
      --expansion <EXPANSION>        The Expander's share of every transition (default: measured on the observed change)
      --isometry <ISOMETRY>          [default: 1.5]
      --prune-factor <PRUNE_FACTOR>  [default: 10]
      --seed <SEED>                  [default: 1]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>              The model file to write (.toml or .json)
  -h, --help                         Print help
subcommands.clue:
CLUE-S (lulcc's CluesModel): logistic regressions, a linear demand, CLUE allocation

Usage: terraflux new clue [OPTIONS] --observed <OBSERVED> --drivers <DRIVERS> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --observed <OBSERVED>            The observed maps, one band per date (the demand is interpolated from them)
      --threads <THREADS>              Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --times <TIMES>                  The date of each band of `observed`, e.g. `0,6,14`
      --drivers <DRIVERS>              The drivers: a raster with one band per variable
      --start <START>                  The map the simulation starts from and the regressions are fitted on (default: the first observed band)
      --formulas <FORMULAS>            The drivers of each class's regression as JSON, e.g. `{"1": ["slope"], "2": ["slope", "dist"]}`
      --elasticity <ELASTICITY>        CLUE: the elasticity of each class (one value, or a list in class order), e.g. `0.2,0.2,0.2`
      --order <ORDER>                  Ordered: the order the classes are served in, e.g. `2,1,3`
      --deterministic                  Ordered: take the most suitable cells instead of drawing them
      --settings <SETTINGS>            The allocation's settings as JSON (CLUE: jitter, scale, max_iter, max_diff, mean_diff)
      --allowed <ALLOWED>              The conversion matrix as JSON, in class order, e.g. `[[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[1,1,1]]`
      --neighbourhood <NEIGHBOURHOOD>  Neighbourhood rules as JSON, e.g. `{"rules": {"1": 0.3, "2": 0.2}}`
      --restrictions <RESTRICTIONS>    A map of restricted cells (non-zero keep their class)
      --history <HISTORY>              A map of the steps each cell has had its class
      --seed <SEED>                    [default: 1]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>                
  -h, --help                           Print help

serve.help:
Run a coordinator: workers ask it for tasks, clients submit batches to it

Usage: terraflux serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --listen <LISTEN>    The address to listen on (127.0.0.1: this machine only; 0.0.0.0:7700 for the network) [default: 127.0.0.1:7700]
      --threads <THREADS>  Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Seconds without news from a worker before its task goes to another [default: 60]
      --data <DATA>        Where the data and the jobs are kept (default: the user's application data); a coordinator started again on it goes on with its jobs
      --code [<CODE>]      A pairing code: TLS, and only the computers given the code (`--code` alone makes one, printed); the coordinator says on the local network where it is, to be found by its code
      --no-beacons         Say nothing on the network (the workers given its address)
  -h, --help               Print help

worker.help:
Run a headless worker: tasks from a coordinator, until stopped

Usage: terraflux worker [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  The coordinator (`host:7700`); with no coordinator, the one of --code found on the network
      --code <CODE>                The coordinator's pairing code (with no --coordinator: the coordinator of the code found on the network)
      --name <NAME>                
      --cache <CACHE>              Where the data of the tasks is kept
      --idle <IDLE>                Take tasks only after this many minutes without the keyboard or the mouse (Windows and macOS)
      --threads <THREADS>          The threads of each task (default: all the cores but one)
  -h, --help                       Print help

submit.help:
Run a batch of a model: replicates (one seed each) or scenarios, here or on a coordinator's workers

Usage: terraflux submit [OPTIONS] <MODEL>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  

Options:
      --replicates <REPLICATES>    Runs with the seeds `--first-seed`, `--first-seed + 1`...
      --threads <THREADS>          Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --first-seed <FIRST_SEED>    [default: 1]
      --scenarios <SCENARIOS>      Scenarios: a TOML file of `[[scenario]] name = "..." set = { "$seed" = 2, "node.setting" = 1.2 }`
      --seed-input <SEED_INPUT>    What holds the seed: an input (`seed`), a node's (`simulation.seed`), or several, separated by commas [default: seed]
  -o, --out <OUT>                  The folder of the results: one folder per task [default: batch]
      --detach                     Only submit the batch to the coordinator and print its job (`terraflux results` fetches it later)
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  The coordinator (`http://host:7700`); without one (and without --code), a coordinator and `--workers` workers run here
      --code <CODE>                The coordinator's pairing code (with no --coordinator: the coordinator of the code found on the network)
      --on <ON>                    A cluster or a server of `terraflux cluster add`: Terraflux started there for the batch, by SSH
      --workers <WORKERS>          Workers on this machine when no coordinator is given (default: a quarter of the cores, at least 1)
  -h, --help                       Print help

calibrate.help:
Calibrate settings of a model against an observed map, here or on a coordinator's workers

Usage: terraflux calibrate [OPTIONS] --param <PARAMS> --observed <OBSERVED> <MODEL>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  The model (.toml or .json)

Options:
      --param <PARAMS>             A setting to vary: `node.setting=from:to` (or `from:to:points`), e.g. `patches.isometry=0.5:2.5`
      --threads <THREADS>          Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --method <METHOD>            `grid` (every combination) or `random` (a Latin hypercube of `--n` draws) [default: grid]
      --n <N>                      Points of each grid range, or draws of a random search [default: 5]
      --seeds <SEEDS>              The seeds each candidate runs with (its score is the mean) [default: 1]
      --observed <OBSERVED>        The observed map at the end of the simulated period: `file.tif` or `file.tif:band`
      --start <START>              The input the simulation starts from [default: t0]
      --metric <METRIC>            What to maximise: `fom` (figure of merit), `overall`, or `similarity:<window>` [default: fom]
      --seed-input <SEED_INPUT>    What holds the seed: an input (`seed`), a node's (`simulation.seed`), or several, separated by commas [default: seed]
  -o, --out <OUT>                  [default: calibration]
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  The coordinator (`http://host:7700`); without one (and without --code), a coordinator and `--workers` workers run here
      --code <CODE>                The coordinator's pairing code (with no --coordinator: the coordinator of the code found on the network)
      --on <ON>                    A cluster or a server of `terraflux cluster add`: Terraflux started there for the batch, by SSH
      --workers <WORKERS>          Workers on this machine when no coordinator is given (default: a quarter of the cores, at least 1)
  -h, --help                       Print help

sensitivity.help:
A global sensitivity analysis of a model's output to its settings (Morris or Sobol, as SALib), here or on a coordinator's workers

Usage: terraflux sensitivity [OPTIONS] --param <PARAMS> --output <OUTPUT> <MODEL>

Arguments:
  <MODEL>  The model (.toml or .json)

Options:
      --param <PARAMS>             A factor and its range: `node.setting=from:to` or `$input=from:to`
      --threads <THREADS>          Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --method <METHOD>            `morris` (elementary effects) or `sobol` (variance-based indices of Saltelli's runs) [default: morris]
      --n <N>                      Morris's trajectories (default 10) or Sobol's base points, a power of 2 (default 64)
      --levels <LEVELS>            Morris's levels of the grid [default: 4]
      --first-order-only           Sobol: only the first and total order indices (factors + 2 runs per base point, not 2 x factors + 2)
      --output <OUTPUT>            The output measured: `node.port` (a number, a table's first row, or a map)
      --statistic <STATISTIC>      Of a map: mean (default), sum, min or max; of a table: its column (default its last)
      --resamples <RESAMPLES>      The bootstraps of the indices' intervals [default: 100]
      --seed <SEED>                The seed of the design and of the bootstraps [default: 1]
      --model-seed <MODEL_SEED>    The seed every run of the model takes [default: 1]
      --seed-input <SEED_INPUT>    What holds the model's seed: an input (`seed`), a node's (`simulation.seed`), or several, separated by commas [default: seed]
  -o, --out <OUT>                  [default: sensitivity]
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  The coordinator (`http://host:7700`); without one (and without --code), a coordinator and `--workers` workers run here
      --code <CODE>                The coordinator's pairing code (with no --coordinator: the coordinator of the code found on the network)
      --on <ON>                    A cluster or a server of `terraflux cluster add`: Terraflux started there for the batch, by SSH
      --workers <WORKERS>          Workers on this machine when no coordinator is given (default: a quarter of the cores, at least 1)
  -h, --help                       Print help

cluster.help:
Clusters and servers reached by SSH: saved once, used by `submit --on`, `calibrate --on`, `results --on`

Usage: terraflux cluster [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add     Save a cluster or a server: `--workers N` (on the host itself) or `--slurm` (on the nodes of an allocation: --nodes, --cpus, --time, --partition, --account, --per-node)
  list    The clusters and servers saved
  test    Check that a cluster is reached and has Terraflux of this version
  stop    Stop Terraflux's coordinator and workers on a cluster (its jobs kept)
  remove  Forget a cluster
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --threads <THREADS>  Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
  -h, --help               Print help

subcommands.add:
Save a cluster or a server: `--workers N` (on the host itself) or `--slurm` (on the nodes of an allocation: --nodes, --cpus, --time, --partition, --account, --per-node)

Usage: terraflux cluster add [OPTIONS] --host <HOST> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  

Options:
      --host <HOST>            `user@host`, or an alias of ~/.ssh/config
      --threads <THREADS>      Threads to use (default: all the cores but one; never every core)
      --ssh-port <SSH_PORT>    
      --program <PROGRAM>      Terraflux there (default: `terraflux` on its PATH, else ~/.terraflux/bin/terraflux)
      --workers <WORKERS>      Workers on the host itself
      --slurm                  Workers on the nodes of a Slurm allocation
      --nodes <NODES>          [default: 1]
      --cpus <CPUS>            The threads of each node used [default: 8]
      --per-node <PER_NODE>    Workers per node [default: 1]
      --time <TIME>            [default: 04:00:00]
      --partition <PARTITION>  
      --account <ACCOUNT>      
  -h, --help                   Print help

cloud-init.help:
The setup script (cloud-init user data) of a machine rented in the cloud: a server with Terraflux (then `terraflux cluster add`), or, with --worker, a machine working for a server's coordinator

Usage: terraflux cloud-init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --worker                     A machine working for a coordinator (its address on the provider's network, --coordinator)
      --coordinator <COORDINATOR>  The coordinator: `host:port`, or the host of a server saved (--on) whose port is taken
      --on <ON>                    The server saved whose coordinator the worker works for (its code and port)
      --code <CODE>                The coordinator's code (without --on)
      --threads <THREADS>          The threads of each task of the worker
      --package <PACKAGE>          Where the Linux package of Terraflux is downloaded from (default: this version's release)
  -h, --help                       Print help
